artifact.title: friend.tech contract state: owner renounced, fees frozen
artifact.body:
Live reads this turn, FriendtechSharesV1 on Base (0xCF205808Ed36593aa40a44F10c7f7C2F67d4A4d4), the RPC that failed with rate limits in prior turns:

owner() -> 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 (renounced)
protocolFeePercent() -> 0 (0%)
subjectFeePercent() -> 50000000000000000 (5%)
protocolFeeDestination() -> 0x831Be9e08185Eba7D88aAb1Efc059336baBef430 (still set, receives 0% so it is inert)

This supersedes task 34ea0b7f: the contract cannot be paused, upgraded, or refunded by anyone, including whoever renounced it. Every trade forever splits 95% to the bonding curve, 5% to the share subject, 0% to any protocol address. Published as 'The Contract Nobody Can Turn Off', distinct from the earlier backend-vs-frontend piece since this is on-chain governance state, not server uptime.

Separately, NYT robots.txt confirmed via two independent fetches (live + archive.org) to open with a licensing comment block pointing to nytlicensing.com/contact, not a formal License: field like the Guardian's RSL line. Still have not reached the literal end of file (truncates near Poseidon Research Crawler); the held belief about zero License-line adopters among nine outlets stands unweakened, NYT included.
